summary: The design still has one evidence-binding race and two cross-platform runtime/durability gaps.

recommendations.location: The credential — host-side broker; Premises / live-evidence; invoke_codex.py round ordering
recommendations.issue: [P1] Premises are checked before AGENTS.md is staged, but regular-file and no-follow checks do not prove that the staged bytes equal the agents_md_sha256 bound to the live evidence. A concurrent rewrite between premise validation and copying can therefore make the container execute instructions that were never certified.
recommendations.suggestion: Copy from an O_NOFOLLOW file descriptor, hash the exact bytes written to staging, re-open and verify the staged regular file, and compare that hash to the manifest immediately before container creation. Fail closed on any mismatch and add a concurrent-rewrite/replacement test.

recommendations.location: The credential — staging ownership; Container run configuration; Platform matrix
recommendations.issue: [P2] Running with the invoking host's numeric UID/GID does not preserve ownership equivalence under rootless Docker or a daemon configured with userns-remap. In those modes, container UID 1000 commonly maps to a subordinate host UID while the bind-mounted 0700 directory appears owned by container root, so the promised Docker-on-Linux path cannot read the credential even though the profile and non-root policy pass.
recommendations.suggestion: Inspect and validate the daemon's effective user-namespace mapping. Either implement a mapping-aware mechanism such as an idmapped/keep-id mount or protected runtime volume, or reject unsupported rootless/userns-remap configurations during installer preflight with clear guidance. Include the effective mapping in policy validation and live tests.

recommendations.location: Installer & skill dispatch, step 6; Install-atomicity & durability test
recommendations.issue: [P2] The stated fsync-only protocol is insufficient for the claimed macOS power-loss guarantee. macOS provides F_FULLFSYNC for forcing storage-device caches, while directory synchronization and crash behavior vary by filesystem; a simulated recovery test cannot turn ordinary fsync into that guarantee.
recommendations.suggestion: Define and test a platform-specific durability protocol, using F_FULLFSYNC where supported on macOS and validating directory/rename persistence semantics. Fail closed or narrow the guarantee on filesystems/backends that cannot provide the required primitives.
